description.en: Ship your AI app to production — learn API wrappers with FastAPI, cost optimization strategies, caching, and monitoring.
description.ta: உங்கள் AI app-ஐ production-க்கு அனுப்புங்கள் — FastAPI உடன் API wrappers, செலவு optimization உத்திகள், caching, monitoring கற்றுக்கொள்ளுங்கள்.

story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Launch Pad

Vaathiyaar stands before a rocket control panel. "Students, building an AI demo is easy. Deploying it for REAL USERS who pay REAL MONEY — that's the challenge. Today you'll learn to wrap your AI in a FastAPI server, optimize costs, add caching, and monitor everything."

### The Production Checklist

1. **API Wrapper** — Wrap your AI logic in a FastAPI endpoint
2. **Cost Control** — Cache responses, use cheaper models when possible
3. **Rate Limiting** — Prevent abuse and control costs
4. **Error Handling** — Graceful fallbacks when the AI API is down
5. **Monitoring** — Track latency, token usage, error rates
6. **Security** — API keys, authentication, input validation

### Cost Optimization Strategies

| Strategy | Savings | Effort |
|----------|---------|--------|
| Cache common queries | 40-60% | Low |
| Use gpt-4o-mini for simple tasks | 90% vs gpt-4o | Low |
| Reduce max_tokens | 10-30% | Low |
| Batch requests | 20-40% | Medium |
| Self-host open-source models | 70-90% | High |

> **Key Insight:** The #1 cost optimization is caching. If 100 users ask the same question, you should call the LLM once and cache the result.

animation_sequence.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from openai import OpenAI

app = FastAPI()
client = OpenAI()

@app.post('/chat')
async def chat(message: str):
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model='gpt-4o-mini',
        messages=[{'role':'user','content': message}],
        max_tokens=200
    )
    return {'reply': response.choices[0].message.content}

# uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
print('AI API ready at http://localhost:8000')

instruction.en: Write the logic behind an AI app's two endpoints (in a real FastAPI app these functions are the bodies of @app.post('/chat') and @app.get('/stats'); the sandbox has no network, so `FakeLLM` stands in for the OpenAI client). `chat(message)`: count the request in stats; if the message is in `cache`, return {"reply": cached reply, "cached": True, "tokens": 0} and count a cache hit; otherwise call `llm.complete(message)`, store the reply in the cache, add its tokens to stats['total_tokens'] and return {"reply": ..., "cached": False, "tokens": ...}. Every request appends {"time": time.time(), "message", "tokens", "cached"} to `request_log`. `get_stats()` returns {"total_requests", "cache_hits", "hit_rate" (hits / requests rounded to 2 decimals, 0.0 when there are no requests), "total_tokens"}.
instruction.ta: ஒரு AI app-இன் இரண்டு endpoints-க்குப் பின்னால் உள்ள logic-ஐ எழுதுங்கள் (உண்மையான FastAPI app-ல் இந்த functions @app.post('/chat') மற்றும் @app.get('/stats')-இன் உடல்களாக இருக்கும்; sandbox-ல் network இல்லாததால் OpenAI client-க்குப் பதிலாக `FakeLLM` உள்ளது). `chat(message)`: request-ஐ stats-ல் எண்ணுங்கள்; message `cache`-ல் இருந்தால் cache hit-ஐ எண்ணி {"reply": cache-ல் உள்ள பதில், "cached": True, "tokens": 0} திருப்புங்கள்; இல்லையெனில் `llm.complete(message)`-ஐ அழைத்து, பதிலை cache-ல் சேமித்து, அதன் tokens-ஐ stats['total_tokens']-ல் கூட்டி {"reply": ..., "cached": False, "tokens": ...} திருப்புங்கள். ஒவ்வொரு request-உம் {"time": time.time(), "message", "tokens", "cached"}-ஐ `request_log`-ல் சேர்க்க வேண்டும். `get_stats()` {"total_requests", "cache_hits", "hit_rate" (hits / requests, 2 தசம இடங்களுக்கு round; requests இல்லையெனில் 0.0), "total_tokens"} திருப்புகிறது.

en: Cache hit: if message in cache: stats['cache_hits'] += 1 and build {'reply': cache[message], 'cached': True, 'tokens': 0}
Cache miss: answer = llm.complete(message); cache[message] = answer['reply']; stats['total_tokens'] += answer['tokens']
get_stats: hit_rate = round(cache_hits / total_requests, 2) if total_requests else 0.0

practice_challenges.test_code:
cache.clear(); request_log.clear(); llm.calls = 0
stats.update(total_requests=0, cache_hits=0, total_tokens=0)
assert get_stats() is not None and get_stats()["hit_rate"] == 0.0, "with no requests yet, hit_rate must be 0.0"
_a = chat("hello there")
assert isinstance(_a, dict), "chat must return a dict"
assert _a.get("cached") is False and _a.get("reply") == "Model answer to: hello there", "a new message must be answered by the model (cached False)"
assert _a.get("tokens") == 7, "tokens must come from llm.complete(...)['tokens']"
_b = chat("hello there")
assert _b.get("cached") is True and _b.get("reply") == _a["reply"] and _b.get("tokens") == 0, "a repeated message must come from the cache with tokens 0"
assert llm.calls == 1, "the model must not be called again for a cached message"
chat("something else")
_s = get_stats()
assert _s == {"total_requests": 3, "cache_hits": 1, "hit_rate": 0.33, "total_tokens": 7 + 7}, "get_stats returned " + repr(_s)
assert len(request_log) == 3, "every request must be logged"
assert all(set(_e) >= {"time", "message", "tokens", "cached"} for _e in request_log), "each log entry needs time, message, tokens and cached"
assert [_e["cached"] for _e in request_log] == [False, True, False], "log entries must record whether the reply was cached"
print("All AI app tests passed!")

under_the_hood.summary: In production each user request passes through your API server, which checks the caller, applies a rate limit, tries a cache, and only then calls the model provider with a timeout and retries, recording tokens and latency on the way out.

steps.title: The server wraps the model call
steps.body: A FastAPI endpoint receives the request, Pydantic validates the body, and your code builds the prompt. The provider's API key stays on the server in an environment variable; the browser never sees it. Because LLM calls take seconds, async handlers let one process serve other requests while it waits.

nodes.label: store in cache, log tokens + latency

steps.title: Rate limiting with a token bucket
steps.body: A common limiter gives each user a bucket of, say, 10 tokens that refills at 1 per second. Each request takes one token; an empty bucket means HTTP 429 'Too Many Requests'. Short bursts are allowed, but sustained traffic is capped at the refill rate, which also caps your spending per user.

steps.title: Caching identical requests
steps.body: The cache key is a hash of everything that affects the answer: model name, prompt text and settings such as temperature. If the same key was answered recently, return the stored response instantly at no model cost. Exact-match caching helps most for repeated questions and deterministic settings.

steps.title: Cost is counted in tokens
steps.body: Providers bill input and output tokens separately, so the cost of a call is input_tokens x input price + output_tokens x output price. Shorter prompts, a max_tokens limit on replies, and routing easy requests to a smaller model reduce both terms. The response's usage field reports the exact counts to log.

steps.title: Retries, fallbacks and monitoring
steps.body: Provider errors such as 429 or 5xx are retried with exponential backoff, waiting about 1, 2, then 4 seconds plus a little randomness so many clients do not retry in sync. After the last retry the app returns a graceful message or switches to a fallback model. Dashboards track latency percentiles, error rate and tokens per day.

under_the_hood.takeaway: The model call is one step in a request pipeline you control. Protect it with authentication and rate limits, avoid it with caching, bound it with timeouts and max_tokens, and measure every call's tokens and latency.
